release.reason: No upstream release tags in the 2026-10-02 source-resolution snapshot.

distribution.reason: Candidate only; actual runtime/source/license and application qualification evidence is pending.

constraints: Linux amd64; libhaskoki.so plus 24 bundled GHC closure libraries and the OpenSSL legacy provider module at ossl-modules/legacy.so ship in-image beside the module ($ORIGIN resolution, no LD_LIBRARY_PATH), with libffi.so.8 vendored from a pinned snapshot .deb behind an ld.so.conf entry. Single token on slot 0; token-present index and native slot ID coincide at 0. The measured glibc floor of this source build is 2.38; the upstream prebuilt artifact's 2.43 floor does not apply.

The adapter always provisions HASKOKI_CONFIG at /var/lib/p11lab/haskoki/haskoki.toml (PIN-free, deterministic): profile real-crypto, sqlite storage at /var/lib/p11lab/haskoki/token.sqlite, engine openssl over OpenSSL 4.0.2 (libcrypto statically linked into the module, so no system libcrypto is used or required, plus the legacy provider module shipped at ossl-modules/legacy.so beside the module, which upstream loads at open), trace disabled. The stored config bytes are verified on every invocation; drift fails as incompatible.

Label policy: slot 0 always serves haskoki-demo; any other P11LAB_LABEL is refused explicitly. Provisioned PINs are the upstream-fixed user 1234 / SO 5678; anything else fails explicitly at initial provisioning (no InitToken/InitPIN/SetPIN path exists upstream). Re-init on complete state is validate-only.

Initialize only an empty writable /var/lib/p11lab volume; compatible init is non-destructive; partial or incompatible state fails. The SQLite store is single-writer: health/readiness never open the module (stock haskoki-ctl config check plus lock-safe SELECT-only store inspection); a second concurrent open fails with the preserved native error.
PIN_FILE/SO_PIN_FILE are preferred; scalar alternatives are explicit disposable-test inputs. Conflicting scalar/file or absent/empty credentials fail initial provisioning.
Ordinary application consumers do not require checker, Python, tracing or a workspace mount. Reset is an explicit removal/replacement of disposable state; no automatic reset or retry.
Whole-image licensing, source companion delivery and digest-bound admission remain separate requirements.
